title: Pureinsure: cheap, but it depends on paid Google ads
subject: Canada life-insurance lead-generation site, live on Flippa (listing 11015517), asking $3,500
price_note: Price shown is the seller's asking price (multiples set to match it).
notes: Asking price is about 3.5 months of the stated profit, which is low enough to suggest a catch.
Revenue comes from Google Ads, so profit depends on ad spend and lead price staying stable; stop paying and the leads stop.
The title says the site is a year old; the listing says 6 years. Ask which is true.
Selling leads to insurers may need a licence in Canada; this screen cannot confirm that. Ask the seller who buys the leads and under what terms.

flags.risk: Ad costs rise or lead buyers pay less
flags.why: Margin of 54% rests on paid traffic

flags.risk: Licensing or compliance problem for lead selling

flags.why: Google Ads accounts have their own rules

questions: Monthly ad spend, leads, price per lead and buyer, for 12 months.
Contracts or terms with each lead buyer.
Is the Google Ads account (with history) included and transferable?
Is the site one year old or six? Show the domain registration date.
Which licence, if any, allows this lead sale, and does it transfer?
How many leads are generated without paid ads?
Refunds or rejected leads in the last 12 months.
What does the CRM cost per month and who owns it?
Why is it priced at about 0.3x profit?
Proof of profit: ad invoices and buyer payments.
